clue.text: Goddess runs into problem coming to wood

indicators.note: the runs abbreviation is set inside the word for a problem, as the clue says it goes into it

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling problem
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A goddess wanders into trouble on reaching a forest, like a figure from myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Proserpine is the Roman name of the queen of the underworld, Greek Persephone.

clue.text: Fairy is something a bit like a mouse

definitions.meaning: the mischievous sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.text: something a bit like a mouse
definitions.meaning: a hand-held pointing device used on graphics tablets, resembling a computer mouse

explanation.surface: A fairy is likened to a small rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's hobgoblin bears this name, and it is also a digitising tool shaped much like a computer mouse.

clue.text: Where nurses are ahead

definitions.meaning: read as two words, nurses work on hospital wards

explanation.surface: Nurses are said to be in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as ON WARDS to see the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean forward in direction or time, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Rare comic, me, performing live? No longer

definitions.text: Rare comic, me, performing live? No longer

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters putting on an act in a new arrangement

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A rare comedian boasts of performing live, then admits those days are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' mixes RARECOMICME with BE. Eric Morecambe, of the British double act Morecambe and Wise, died in 1984, hence 'No longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A much-loved British comedian, now dead, so a rare comic who can perform live no longer.

clue.text: A cook opening up Eastern building

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to do food is to cook it
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: A chef opens up a building in the East, perhaps a new restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower or temple found in East Asia.

clue.text: Put up message about mother keeping home

indicators.note: the word for a message goes about, that is around, the rest

parts.note: a note is a short message

indicators.note: the word for mother keeps the home word inside it

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
in means at home

explanation.surface: A note about mother staying home is put on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up for a post is to propose them as a candidate, a synonym.

clue.text: Restrain dog beginning to bark

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: beginning to bark points to the opening letter of that word

explanation.surface: An owner checks a dog as it starts to bark.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb something is to hold it in check, a synonym.

clue.text: Free houseplant ordered without pot

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order
without says the letters of pot are taken out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone buys a houseplant but orders it with no pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P, O and T from HOUSEPLANT and 'ordered' rearranges the remaining HUSELAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To free a dog or a force is to let it loose, a synonym.

clue.text: Uninteresting one sent packing must be buttered up

parts.note: bland means dull or uninteresting
I is the Roman numeral one
to shed staff is to get rid of them, send them packing

explanation.surface: A dull employee who has been dismissed must be flattered on the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax with flattery, so buttered up is a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Something on the moors found by farm animal for cover

indicators.note: found by places the moorland plant right beside the animal, after it

parts.note: a cow is a farm animal
ling is heather, which grows on moorland

explanation.surface: A walker finds something on the moors by a cow and uses it for shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowling is a removable metal covering over an engine.

clue.text: Some dull academic putting outsiders off — a bit of a brain

indicators.note: take the outside letters off the run of words and what is inside them remains

explanation.surface: A boring scholar alienates outsiders, though they are a bit of a brain.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the S of 'Some' and the C of 'academic' to read the letters in between.
explanation.definitionFit: The medulla oblongata is the lowest part of the brainstem, a part of the brain.

clue.text: Nice coda tails off in a series of notes

indicators.note: off means the letters have gone wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fine coda peters out in a run of notes, as in a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatonic scale is a seven-note musical scale of tones and semitones, so a series of notes.

clue.text: Proper fuss' preceding heartless sister, a drama queen

indicators.note: preceding puts the first two words ahead of the rest

parts.note: prim means primly proper
ado is fuss

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter from the word for a religious sister

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A proper fuss is made before a cold nun by someone over-dramatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna, originally an opera's lead soprano, is a temperamental, self-important person.

clue.text: Girl with male doing a bunk gets welfare

indicators.note: British slang for running off, so the male abbreviation leaves

parts.note: a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl whose man has run off is now on benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a bunk' is British slang for fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid is help or assistance, as welfare is.

clue.text: Awfully boorish chap with nothing to lose becoming a prelate

indicators.note: awfully means the letters are rearranged in an awful way
to lose says the letter for nothing is lost from the mix

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rude fellow who has nothing to lose is promoted to high church office.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one O from BOORISHCHAP and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior bishop is a church dignitary, which is what a prelate is.

clue.text: Relax with men in haunt

indicators.note: the men abbreviation goes in the word for relax

parts.note: to rest is to relax
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: People unwind with friends at a favourite hangout.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a place one goes to often, as a haunt is.

clue.text: Bad mood demonstrated by the man's poetic pieces

parts.note: a strop is a sulky bad temper
he's is short for he is, the man is

explanation.surface: A poet's verses show off his foul temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Strophes are stanzas or sections of a poem.

clue.text: Unpreferred female? Superior but losing right to keep career

indicators.note: the shortened word keeps the career word inside
losing removes the right letter from the word for superior

parts.note: better means superior
to career is to rush along, run

explanation.surface: A woman passed over is superior but loses her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' and 'to keep' are the two operations. The film title Gentlemen Prefer Blondes makes a dark-haired woman 'Unpreferred'.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful definition from the saying that gentlemen prefer blondes, making a dark-haired woman unpreferred.

clue.text: Group refusing to give something for foundation

definitions.meaning: the unyielding central group who will not compromise
broken brick and stone used as a base for roads

explanation.surface: A group will not concede anything in return for a base.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both stubborn diehards and rubble laid under roads as a base.

clue.text: Wandered here and there, taking walk into road

indicators.note: the walk word goes into the road abbreviation

parts.note: to amble is to walk slowly

explanation.surface: Someone strolled about, taking a walk onto a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramble is to roam aimlessly, wandering here and there.

clue.text: The paper lies?

parts.note: a fabric of falsehoods is called a ... of lies, and a soft thin paper bears the same name

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether the newspaper is lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin soft paper, and a web of untruths is a tissue of lies.

clue.text: Mirrors broken in capsule

indicators.note: broken means the letters of capsule are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Mirrors are smashed inside a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: Specula is the plural of speculum, a mirror, especially a metal one in a telescope.

clue.text: Maidenly, showing cold briskness

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps
haste is brisk speed

explanation.surface: A maiden shows a chilly, brusque manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and virginal, as maidenly suggests.

clue.text: Distinctive practice of religion US city neglected

indicators.note: neglected means the city is left out of the religion

parts.note: Islam is a religion
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A religion's distinctive practice is ignored by an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is a distinctive doctrine or practice, as in any word ending in that suffix.

clue.text: City fellow with salute across street

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: the salute word lies across the street abbreviation, around it

parts.note: a cheer is a salute

explanation.surface: A man waves to someone across the road in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester is a large city in north-west England.

clue.text: Editor laid into this writer who proverbially laid down the law

definitions.text: who proverbially laid down the law

indicators.note: the editor abbreviation is laid into, placed inside, the word for this writer

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: An editor attacked the writer who was always dictating rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid into' looks like an attack. The laws of the Medes and Persians are proverbially unalterable.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of ancient Media, whose laws with the Persians' were proverbially unchangeable.

clue.text: Most sacred element of Mass conveying story

indicators.note: the Mass word carries the story word within it

parts.note: the host is the consecrated bread of the Mass
a lie is a story, a fib

explanation.surface: Part of the Mass carries a holy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of holy, most sacred.

clue.text: King is featured in piece of sculpture in standing

indicators.note: featured in puts the king abbreviation inside the sculpture word

parts.note: a statue is a piece of sculpture
R is for rex, Latin king

explanation.surface: A king appears in a standing statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is reputation or eminence, one's standing.

clue.text: Notice son going behind soft cushions

indicators.note: going behind puts the notice and son pieces after the soft letter

parts.note: P is piano, soft in music
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: A son spots soft cushions behind him.
explanation.definitionFit: Pads are soft cushioning pieces, a synonym.

clue.text: Give new life to undisciplined teenager joining branch of Army

indicators.note: joining sets the two pieces side by side

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a branch of the British Army

indicators.note: undisciplined means the letters of teenager run wild

explanation.surface: An unruly teenager is given a fresh start by enlisting.
explanation.definitionFit: To regenerate is to renew or revive, giving new life.
